cards.text: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD comes to the prophet Ezekiel, and he's the one telling it. He knows the EXACT day. Friend, I have to check my phone to find out it's Thursday.
God calls him "son of man" and gives him news about the multitudes of Egypt. Egypt is on its way out, and this is NOT good news.

cards.question: With news that heavy, what does God tell Ezekiel to do for the multitudes of Egypt?
Egypt is going down, along with the daughters of the mighty nations. Where is God sending them?

answers.text: To the depths of the earth
To an island in the sea
To the far side of the desert

cards.text: Then God asks Egypt, "Whom do you surpass in beauty?" And right after that: "Go down and be placed with the uncircumcised!"

cards.question: God asks Egypt, "Whom do you surpass in beauty?" and then tells her to go down with the rest. What is He telling Egypt?

answers.text: She is no better than the rest
She will rise above the others

cards.text: I was the shiniest stamper on the counter, then BOOM, back of the junk drawer with a pile of dead batteries. For Egypt it's far more serious: they will fall among those slain by the sword, and God says, let them drag her away with all her multitudes.

cards.question: Right in the middle of it, God declares, "The ___ is appointed!"

cards.text: From the middle of Sheol, mighty chiefs speak up about Egypt and her allies. I picture the whole room looking up, like when the new hire walks into the office.

cards.question: Down in Sheol, what do the mighty chiefs say about Egypt and her allies?

answers.text: They have come down to lie with the slain
They have escaped the sword this time
They are too strong to come down here

cards.text: Then the message walks us through who's already down there. First up is Assyria, with her whole company and her graves all around her.

cards.question: Assyria's company now lies slain in the depths of the Pit. What did they once do in the land of the living?
Next in the Pit is Elam, with all her multitudes around her grave, slain by the sword. True or false: down there, Elam is honored for the terror she once spread.

cards.text: Among the slain, they prepare a resting place for Elam and all her hordes. Then Meshech and Tubal are there too, with all their multitudes and their graves all around them.
Then the text brings up the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war. Their swords were placed under their heads, and their shields rested on their bones.

cards.question: True or false: Meshech and Tubal lie down with those fallen warriors of old.
Then the message turns to "you" and says "you" will be shattered too. Where will "you" lie down?
Edom is there too, with all her kings and princes, who despite their ___ are laid among those slain by the sword.

cards.text: All the leaders of the north and all the Sidonians are there too, gone down in disgrace with the slain. Now picture Pharaoh arriving and looking around at every one of them.

cards.question: When Pharaoh sees all these nations in the Pit, what does God say happens to him?

answers.text: He will cry out for help

cards.text: Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, and he's COMFORTED. I think that's like getting a parking ticket and feeling better because the WHOLE street got one.

cards.question: Then God has the last word, and the line about terror in the land of the living comes back one more time. Whose terror is it now?

cards.text: So Pharaoh and all his multitude will be laid to rest among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD. Every mighty nation on that list, and God gets the last word.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "son of man", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "The ___ is appointed!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card spends all three sentences on the date and a joke about the date. It never says what is going on: a word from the LORD about Egypt, coming in the middle of Ezekiel's messages against Egypt.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "Where is God sending them?" In 32:18, God tells Ezekiel to consign Egypt and the daughters of the mighty nations to the depths of the earth. The card makes God the one doing the sending.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answers "To an island in the sea" and "To the far side of the desert" are generic places, not real details from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: "I was the shiniest stamper on the counter, then BOOM" contradicts his backstory. He was worn down, his edges went soft and his stamps blurred before he was replaced. It was gradual, and he was never the shiniest. The line adds something new to his story that the story itself contradicts.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 7 has just told the baker that Egypt will "fall among those slain by the sword." The very next card then asks the baker to fill "sword" into "The ___ is appointed!" The earlier card gives the answer away. The blank also tests the exact wording of a line instead of meaning.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 4 multiple choice cards, 1 fill in the blank and no true or false. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card is only a bare restatement of the two quotes in 32:19, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 6 then repeats the same quote.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 2 (cards 1, 4, 5 and 13) are flat summaries of the verses with no reactions, disbelief or comparisons. Only card 11 has a real laugh. The stop reads like a plain list of the verses, not like Papa Dorin telling them.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: None of the nations get a simple identification when they first show up: Assyria (stop 2 card 1), Elam (stop 2 card 3), Meshech and Tubal (stop 2 card 4), Edom (stop 2 card 8), and the leaders of the north and the Sidonians (stop 2 card 9). Pharaoh is also never identified as Egypt's king (stop 2 card 9).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word "might" in a line they haven't seen. "Kings and princes, who despite their wealth" would fit just as well, so the answer can't be reasoned out from meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
